plan.family: A (3-SAT, n=16, ratio 4.0); all other settings as in the reported study
plan.primary_metric: faith_excess_id (density-controlled clause-F1 excess, ID split, final model)

C1_convergence.note: 4x the calibrated budget (12 epochs); same cosine schedule stretched to 48 epochs; the FINAL model is evaluated (no early stopping, no model selection); learning curve of the ID excess on the first 512 ID instances every 6 epochs (reporting only)

C2_rl.estimator: RLOO score-function gradient (4 formula samples per instance from the translator's per-slot categorical distribution; leave-one-out baseline); no gradient passes through any solver
C2_rl.reward: class-balanced agreement between the EXACT entailment labels of the sampled formula and the gold labels over the instance's queries (label True/False/Unknown as in the follow-up study; weights = inverse gold-label frequency over the training set); exact labels by exhaustive enumeration of the 2^16 assignments
C2_rl.loss: task_weight * -(advantage * log-probability of the sampled formula, i.e. the sum over its slots; standard REINFORCE/RLOO), averaged over samples and instances; task_weight = 1; per-slot loss, density hinge and logit penalty as in `frozen`

rl_ans_ps[Q=1].note: same single query per instance as A1/A2

rl_ans_ps[Q=16].note: one query per variable, polarity from default_rng(1)

C3_shuffled_answers.labels: the follow-up study's answer labels permuted across training instances (numpy default_rng(2)); class weights unchanged
C3_shuffled_answers.note: tests whether the A2 harm comes from the answer content or from adding a loss

C1.claim: with training to convergence, routing the solver gradient improves ID excess under scarce per-slot supervision

C2.claim: answer feedback from an exact solver without differentiation improves ID excess under scarce per-slot supervision

C3.claim: the A2 harm is caused by the answer content: shuffled labels harm less

plan.confirmatory_rule: one-sided exact sign-flip permutation test on the 12 per-seed differences (all 2^12 sign patterns); Holm over {C1, C2, C3} at alpha = 0.05; SUPPORTED iff Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 AND mean difference >= 0.03
plan.secondary: success indicator (faith_excess_id > 0.30): exact one-sided McNemar; hurdle summary (success counts; mean excess of successful and failed runs); non-superiority: a benefit >= 0.03 is excluded iff the upper limit of the t-based 90% interval of the mean difference is < 0.03
plan.convergence_criterion: C1 is called converged if, averaged over seeds, the ID excess on the first 512 ID instances changes by less than 0.02 between epochs 36 and 48 in both conditions
plan.diagnostic: rl_ans_ps[Q=16] vs frozen and vs rl_ans_ps[Q=1] (seeds 0-5); rl_ans[Q=16] vs the follow-up study's A1 runs (seeds 0-5); estimates with 95% t intervals and exact two-sided sign-flip p-values, no verdicts
